summary: E2E testing of invitation + set-password + change-password feature. Backend: 20/21 pytest tests passing. Frontend: all critical UI flows (set-password valid/invalid, mismatched pw error, redirect to login, users page create/badge/resend, change-password wrong+correct flows) PASS. Two real bugs found: (1) user_invited activity log is skipped when Resend fails, (2) Cloudflare intercepts 502 responses from /resend-invitation & /send-password-reset and returns a generic HTML error page — the admin will NOT see the clear backend error message on that path (only the create-user 200-with-email_error path shows the Resend detail in UI, which we visually confirmed works well).

critical.issue: activity_logs entry 'user_invited' is skipped when the invitation email fails. log_activity is placed INSIDE the try-block after send_invitation_email, so any Resend failure (very common with fake emails and expected per PRD) means the invitation is NEVER logged. Requirement said 'Cada envío se registra en activity_logs'. Move log_activity out of the try (or log both success + failure explicitly).

When Resend fails, backend raises HTTPException 502 with a clear JSON detail. However, in this preview environment Cloudflare intercepts any 5xx response from the origin and replaces the body with its own generic HTML 'Bad Gateway' page. Result: the admin toast will show something like 'Error 502' with no useful detail. In contrast, POST /api/users handles the Resend failure by returning 200 with {email_sent:false, email_error:'...'}, and the UsersPage shows the full Resend error message in a nice toast (confirmed visually). Recommendation: apply the same pattern to /resend-invitation and /send-password-reset — return 200 (or 4xx with a non-5xx code such as 424/409) with a JSON body {sent:false, error:'<Resend detail>'} instead of raising HTTPException(502). This is the only way admins will see the clear error text as required by decision (4).

integration_issues.flow: Resend invitation / password reset error surface
integration_issues.issue: Because of the Cloudflare 502 hijack above, the toast after clicking the resend/reset button in UsersPage will not contain the Resend error detail. During our test we saw an error-looking toast but the full text ('You can only send testing emails to your own email address...') was NOT preserved — unlike the 'Crear y Enviar Invitación' flow which DID surface the full Resend text (great UX in that path).

action_items: Move log_activity('user_invited', ...) OUTSIDE the try-block in POST /api/users (server.py ~line 4856) so the invitation is recorded even when Resend rejects.

Change POST /api/users/{id}/resend-invitation and POST /api/users/{id}/send-password-reset to return a non-5xx JSON with {sent:false, error:<detail>} (or use 424/409) instead of raising HTTPException(502). Cloudflare hijacks 5xx and prevents the clear error message from reaching the admin. Update the frontend toast to render error from that field.
(Optional polish) After the above fix, mirror UsersPage's 'Usuario creado, pero el email de invitación NO se pudo enviar…' toast pattern for the resend/reset actions.

email_service._send raises RuntimeError if RESEND_API_KEY or SENDER_EMAIL are missing, and Resend SDK raises resend.exceptions.ResendError which propagates cleanly with the useful detail — this is why the create-user path can surface a friendly message.

It uses ATLAS_URI/ATLAS_DB_NAME with fallback to MONGO_URL/DB_NAME. It creates users with @testing-fake-domain.com (pydantic EmailStr rejects .local TLD). Note that Cloudflare masks all 5xx backend responses in this preview env — do not assert on the JSON body of 502 responses, only on the status code.

rca of the issue.user_invited_missing: In server.py the block at ~4854-4859 puts both send_invitation_email(...) AND await log_activity(current_user,'user_invited',...) inside the same try. Any exception from Resend jumps to the except branch, so the log line is never reached. Fix: move log_activity out (either before the try, or in a finally / after email_sent computation).
rca of the issue.cloudflare_502_hijack: The resend/reset endpoints raise fastapi HTTPException(status_code=502, detail='...'). The upstream Cloudflare edge that fronts the preview domain has 5xx interception enabled — it replaces the origin body with its own HTML error page. Consequence: r.json() at the client raises JSONDecodeError, and the admin toast can't render backend detail. Fix suggestion: keep endpoint 2xx and return {sent:false, error:<detail>} following the same pattern already implemented in POST /api/users (which was observed to display the full 'You can only send testing emails to your own email address...' string beautifully in the UI).
